q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ID) >1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ID) >1
explanation: Q1 checks for duplicate emails by counting the occurrences of each email in the PERSON table and returning those with more than one occurrence. Q2, on the other hand, groups the table by the first column (EMAIL) and checks if there are multiple distinct IDs for each email. The difference arises because Q2 uses COUNT(DISTINCT ID) to determine duplicates, which is not the same as checking the count of the email itself.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two rows with the same email but different IDs to trigger the difference between Q1 and Q2.
